hook.line: Hernando leaves a message with Vale: "he says you're coming" or "he says you should come"? One ending apart, and the plans change completely.
hook.en: He says you're coming tomorrow. (to a friend)

rule:
*Decir que* can mean two things, and the verb after it tells you which.

If you are passing on **news**, the verb stays in its normal form (*vienes*, *está*, *trabajo*). It is a fact.

If you are passing on an **order or a wish**, the verb takes the "opposite" ending (*vengas*, *cierres*, *trabaje*). It is something that should happen.

*Dice que vienes* = he says you are coming.
*Dice que vengas* = he says to come.

English says "he says..." in both cases. In Spanish, listen to the last letter.
smallPrint: Teachers call this indicative for information and subjunctive for influence, both after *decir que*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose the right form and type the whole sentence (He says you're coming tomorrow. To a friend): Dice que ___ mañana. (vienes / vengas)
yourTurn.why: You are passing on news, so the verb stays normal: *vienes*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose the right form and type the whole sentence (He says to come tomorrow. To a friend): Dice que ___ mañana. (vienes / vengas)
Type in Spanish: Vale says the café is closed.
yourTurn.answer: Vale dice que el café está cerrado.
yourTurn.why: A fact keeps its normal verb: *está*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish (to a friend): Vale says for you to close the café.
yourTurn.answer: Vale dice que cierres el café.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: My mom says I work a lot.
yourTurn.answer: Mi mamá dice que trabajo mucho.
yourTurn.why: News about me: *trabajo*, the normal form.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it an order: Mi mamá dice que trabajo mucho. (My mom says I should work less)
yourTurn.answer: Mi mamá dice que trabaje menos.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it news: Dile que llame mañana. (Tell him I'll call tomorrow)
yourTurn.why: You are telling him a fact about you, so *llamo*.

pitfalls.wrong: Mi mamá dice que trabajo menos.
pitfalls.right: Mi mamá dice que trabaje menos.
pitfalls.why: Almost. An order uses the "opposite" ending, *trabaje*, not *trabajo*.
To tell someone to come you need the request ending: *venga*.

pitfalls.wrong: Vale dice que cierre a las seis.
pitfalls.right: Vale dice que cierra a las seis.
pitfalls.why: If it is just a fact about the café, keep the normal verb: *cierra*.

personal: Think of a message someone gave you this week. Write it twice: once as news (*dice que...*) and once as an order (*dice que...* with a changed ending).
